extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of political philosophy (readers of Plato's Republic)
extracted.subtask_short: designing a guardian class for a utopia
extracted.subtask_description: Normative prescriptions for organizing and maintaining an ideal guardian class and polity: criteria for selection, education, family structure, breeding, rewards/punishments, and wartime conduct. Focus is on communal arrangements that promote unity and the common good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal education and shared pursuits for men and women
rubrics_metrics.description: The same education which makes a man a good guardian will make a woman a good guardian; women and men ought to have the same pursuits (music, gymnastics, administration) except where physical differences legitimately alter task distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose education by aptitude rather than sex; do not exclude women from guardianship tasks simply because of gender. Example: women who have turns for gymnastic, military exercises, or philosophy shall be trained alongside men. Anti-pattern: assuming childbearing alone determines women's education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of guardians by natural gifts, not sex
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians are to be selected for qualities of soul and capacity; those women who possess guardian-qualities are to be selected as companions and colleagues of men with similar qualities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment should look for natural aptitude (spirit, temper, capacity for administration), not merely social role. Selection pairs those of like capacity and character regardless of sex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community of wives and children (common families)
rubrics_metrics.description: The wives of the guardians are to be common, and their children are to be common, and no parent is to know his own child, nor any child his parent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement communal marriage/childcare to produce unity of feeling and prevent private ‘mine/not mine’ divisions. The text treats this as both highly beneficial to the State and highly controversial in possibility. Exceptions for sanctioned lots/oracles may be permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common property and no private possessions for guardians
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians were not to have houses or lands or any other property; their pay was to be their food, provided by other citizens — they are to have no private expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to remove causes of quarrel and rivalry (wealth, possessions, private households). This supports unity and prevents suits/complaints arising from property or familial disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlled eugenic-style breeding and population management
rubrics_metrics.description: The best of either sex should be united with the best as often, and the inferior with the inferior as seldom as possible; the rulers will regulate the number of weddings and take account of wars/diseases to preserve the population average.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulers should arrange festivals and mating occasions, breed from those of 'ripe age' only, and use lots/secret measures to disguise manipulation. This includes the use of officers to collect offspring and dispose of deformed or inferior births. The guidance endorses secrecy and administrative discretion to maintain 'first-rate' condition of guardians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age windows for sanctioned reproduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined 'prime' reproductive ages: women begin at about twenty and continue until forty; men begin at twenty-five and continue until about fifty-five. Sexual relations and childbearing outside these sanctioned ages/counts are deemed unholy or illegitimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce age restrictions at public hymeneals; offspring conceived outside sanctioned occasions are to be treated as uncertified and not maintained by the State. Incestuous unions after prime are explicitly prohibited (e.g., father/daughter, mother/son).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous assignment and naming of offspring to prevent parental partiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Children born after a hymeneal are to be called sons or daughters of the bridegroom present at the hymn (by dating births to seventh/tenth months after the hymeneal), and no one will truly know biological parentage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This naming scheme keeps parentage secret, prevents familial loyalties, and forbids intermarriage among those deemed siblings by timing. Exception: if the lot favors marriage and an oracle sanctions it, some prohibitions may be lifted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communal upbringing and professional wet-nursing
rubrics_metrics.description: Offspring are taken to communal pens/folds and cared for by nurses in a separate quarter; mothers come to nurse when milk is needed but do not recognize their own children and do not nurse for prolonged periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design institutions (nurses, separate quarters) to ensure children are reared collectively. Aim to prevent maternal partiality and maintain the communal character of family life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of labour by relative physical strength
rubrics_metrics.description: In distribution of labours the lighter are to be assigned to the women, who are the weaker natures, but in other respects their duties are to be the same as men's; women also share in war and defence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign tasks pragmatically by strength while maintaining equality of civic duties. Women to participate in gymnastic and military training, but account for physical differences in task assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of rulers' obedience and auxiliaries' command
rubrics_metrics.description: For rulers and auxiliaries, there must be willingness to obey in the one and the power of command in the other; guardians must obey laws and imitate their spirit in entrusted details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate both legal obedience and internalized respect for laws among guardians. Leadership requires both the capacity to command and the moral disposition to submit to the law when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of regulated falsehoods (noble lies) as political medicine
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulers will often have to practise upon the body corporate with medicines: a considerable dose of falsehood and deceit [is] necessary for the good of their subjects; such lawful use of falsehood seems likely to be often needed in regulations of marriages and births.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat certain public myths or secret manipulations as therapeutic for societal cohesion — but exercise caution: these deceptions are to be administered by rulers for salutary ends and kept secret to avoid unrest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children as early spectators/helpers of war, with safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Children should be spectators of war and sometimes helpers (carrying out safe tasks) so they learn their future duties; take them on safe expeditions, place them under veteran leaders, and mount them on horses early so they can escape if danger arises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance exposure to martial life with child safety: select safe campaigns for observation, use tractable swift horses, and put children under experienced commanders. Purpose: habituation to warcraft and incentive to valour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honouring and rewarding bravery (gender-neutral honours)
rubrics_metrics.description: Brave soldiers (men or women) are to be honoured with hymns, distinctions, seats of precedence, meats and cups; specific honors include crowns, the right hand of fellowship, kissing, and privileges in mating/offspring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use public honors and material privileges to incentivize courage and service. Examples from tradition (Homer, Hesiod) are invoked as models. Preference in mating/childbearing may be among the rewards given to the brave to increase offspring of valorous stock.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punishment for cowardice and reward of distinguished heroism
rubrics_metrics.description: A soldier who deserts his rank or acts cowardly should be degraded to a husbandman or artisan; one who allows himself to be taken prisoner may be given to the enemies; conversely, the distinguished hero receives honour and social rewards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ clear, reputationally severe penalties for cowardice to maintain military discipline, and publicly reward heroism to model virtues for youth and the polity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid enslaving/killing/despoiling fellow Hellenes
rubrics_metrics.description: No Hellene should be owned as a slave by other Hellenes; conquerors ought to take only the armour and must abstain from spoiling the dead or hindering burial. Devastation or burning of Hellenic houses should be forbidden; at most annual produce may be taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between war against barbarians (external enemy) and discord among Hellenes (internal disorder). Preserve kinship and unity among Hellenes by sparing them enslavement and ritual despoilment; avoid actions that prolong discord.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity through community of pleasures and pains
rubrics_metrics.description: The greatest good is unity: there is unity where there is community of pleasures and pains — where citizens are glad or grieved on the same occasions; community of women, children, and property fosters this unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize social institutions (communal families, shared property, collective rites) to align citizens' affective responses so the State resembles a single organism feeling together. Measure a well-ordered State by the degree citizens internalize common joys/sorrows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of petty meannesses and lawsuits
rubrics_metrics.description: Without private property or separate households, citizens are delivered from flattery of the rich, burdens of family maintenance, borrowing/repudiating, and many other meannesses; suits and complaints will have no existence among them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce incentives for petty social conflicts by removing economic sources (private property, familial inheritance). The expectation is that equality and communal living diminish petty injustices and legal disputes.
